## Smallest closable capability

A caller supplies canonical source identity/shape and a URL/Request locator. One successful cold install reads one 200 full GET containing MISOSTM1, sequentially decodes its packed native FLAC chunks through the existing controller, maps packed frames to timeline spans, and lets VerifiedSparsePcmStore commit only after transport/chunk/full-canonical verification. Warm verified open invokes neither locator nor decoder. Reuse accepted session/pump/storage APIs; no new install coordinator, cache format, session controller or dense fallback.

Preparation downloads every byte of each required asset before it can be ready. All unique sources must complete through accepted openSession/openSparseEngineWebSession before session readiness. This issue provides an indexed acquisition primitive, not a durable offline-library claim: app shell/session snapshots, deletion lifetime ownership, offline presentation and final deployment remain separate. Decode happens during preparation only; warm playback reads the existing sparse PCM cache.

## Concrete public boundary

Export from /stems only:

```ts
export type SparseStemLocator = (
  identity: StemIdentity,
  options: { readonly signal: AbortSignal },
) => string | URL | Request | Promise<string | URL | Request>;

export interface SparseStemDeliveryOptions extends Pick<FlacDeliveryOptions,
  "fetch" | "readDeadlineMs" | "decodeNoProgressMs" | "admission" |
  "memoryBudgetBytes" | "maximumWorkers" | "hardwareConcurrency" |
  "deviceMemory" | "assets" | "createWorker"
> {
  readonly locate: SparseStemLocator;
}

export function createSparseStemResolver(
  options: SparseStemDeliveryOptions,
): (expected: SparsePcmExpectation, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<SparsePcmResolved>;
```

No Range attempt, maximumAttempts or processing/hash-trust option is exposed by this new API. One call is one attempt; caller retry means a new complete operation. Reuse current option validation/defaults and snapshot worker/asset hooks before use. No worker or request starts at factory creation. Public failures retain EngineWebAdapterError codes/details and complete causal information.

The returned function plugs directly into `SparsePcmSessionOptions.resolve` and `SparseEngineWebSessionOptions.resolver`. Standalone install uses `store.installSource(expected, {resolve: signal => resolve(expected, signal)})`. It returns the existing `{spans: AsyncIterable<SparsePcmSpan>}`; omit the optional index in this first slice because the store derives it and compares the full canonical hash. The manifest remains authoritative only for transport mapping after exact binding to expected; it cannot replace expected identity/shape. No new span/source descriptor types or public generic byte-source/worker framework.

Acquisition is lazy at first iterator pull, allowing return/cancellation before first pull without opening resources. The single-consumer span iterator owns one scoped acquisition through EOF/return/error and releases borrowed blocks when the next pull confirms consumption, or during return/error. Store's accepted iterator ownership already waits for physical settlement. An already aborted signal refuses before locator/worker work.

## One HTTP cursor and finite chunk sources

Use Effect4.0.0-rc.112 HttpClient/FetchHttpClient with one response scope alive through actual EOF or cancellation. Existing fetch override is an actual transport dependency; no fake Range/Response implementation. Normalize locator Request to bodyless GET, preserve established caller credentials/cache/referrer policy, replace its signal with the composed operation signal, and remove Range and If-Range under this documented full-GET contract. Require200 and a body; reject206 and other statuses before decode. No HEAD or preliminary GET, no per-chunk requests, no body retry/resume, no tee/background body collection.

Acquire existing bounded download admission once for the entire response, including time waiting for sequential chunks, output and store backpressure. Do not release/reacquire it per chunk or use the same single permit recursively for decoder admission. Share the existing pool/admission implementation across calls to one resolver, with at most one active worker lease per source and one fresh worker per chunk. Workers terminate before the next chunk lease; no reset/reinitialize optimization.

Content-Length is optional. An exposed value must be a valid nonnegative safe integer matching the exact admitted header+manifest+payload length. Missing/inaccessible length is allowed; actual byte counts and final EOF are authoritative. Accept absent or visible identity Content-Encoding; reject any visible other encoding before decoding. Browser header visibility is a caller/CDN representation contract, not proof that an inaccessible header is absent. Do not attempt to set forbidden Accept-Encoding or compare encoded transfer length to decoded representation length. No CDN change is required; public CDN observations are contextual evidence, not a runtime prerequisite.

Freeze the accepted transport-view ceiling at1MiB: reject a returned body Uint8Array with byteLength OR retained ArrayBuffer.byteLength exceeding1MiB before copying, joining or retaining it. This is an adapter admission limit, not a Fetch guarantee. Keep at most one accepted carry view and one <=256KiB delivery scratch buffer; inspect incoming views before creating any aggregate buffer. A too-large transport chunk is a typed refusal even if total object size is otherwise valid. Browser/network internal allocations remain outside this package bound. Test exactly-at-limit, over-limit and small view over oversized backing buffer. Metadata gets its separate <=8MiB manifest allocation after header preflight; do not assemble payload/chunk ArrayBuffers or Blobs.

Read exactly16 bytes and use `admitSparseStemHeader`; then read exactly admitted manifestBytes and use `admitSparseStemManifest` plus `assertSparseStemSessionBinding(manifest, expected)`. Reuse all accepted interval/chunk/object caps: <=65536 records per array, <=8MiB exact canonical manifest, <=32MiB encoded and <=30 seconds packed frames per chunk, <=8GiB object, launch rates and exactly1|2 channels/16|24 bits. Counts and lengths are checked before growth/Schema traversal. Byte cursor offsets are checked safe integers. No second manifest validator.

Preserve accepted eight-byte magic exactly: ASCII `MISOSTM1`, hex `4d 49 53 4f 53 54 4d 31`. Existing header admission validates all eight bytes. No format correction is needed. Unknown/truncated magic and native fLaC refuse here without parser fallback. Successor C adds positive native dispatch from the same GET prefix.

Each chunk supplies a private DecoderByteSource over only its declared encoded extent. Its actual accepted66 failure type is DecoderByteSourceError, not EngineWebAdapterError; preserve the tagged prepare/read/finish operation and original cause. Accepted66 passes `DecoderByteSourceOptions.borrow = { adopt(release), release() }` into the source factory. Real ranged delivery adopts ownership before acquisition/progress callbacks; the new finite cursor must likewise adopt any source-visible borrowed bytes synchronously before a yield, callback or abort can discard their return value. Use that one controller-operation owner, already protected by the input scope finalizer; release/clear after metadata use or input-slot copy, and during finish/error/interruption. Do not register one finalizer per historical read, defer adoption to the controller after source.read returns, or permit a new cursor read/scratch overwrite while the current borrow is live. The outer response scope owns its carry view/body reader; the per-decode owner covers the current source-visible lease, not the entire HTTP response. prepare reads STREAMINFO and scans/skips remaining metadata sequentially in bounded slices, hashing all bytes including magic/metadata; retain <=128 metadata-block bound and existing decoder block restrictions. Expected sample count/PCM byte count are CHUNK values, while rate/channels/depth match the full source. read obeys existing input credits <=256KiB and never crosses into the next chunk. finish drains/hashes the finite unread suffix without waiting for another worker credit, then verifies exact extent and flacSha256. Cursor ownership serializes prepare/read/finish; no concurrent body reads.

## Minimal private controller adaptation

Use accepted66's single input lane/controller. Its current `createFlacStemResolverWithSource(options: FlacDeliveryOptions, sourceFactory)` is still a test-only module export, absent from package entrypoints; `makeFlacStemResolver` still requires locate and constructs range delivery. It is not yet a ready production full-response entry. Extract/factor a narrow private invocation of that same controller accepting a source factory with borrow ownership, parent identity, chunk decode context and shared pool resources. Keep range-specific options/construction in the legacy wrapper, so B supplies neither a dummy locate/range callback nor a fake response. Do not expose DecoderByteSourceOptions.range as a requirement of the finite source. Preserve legacy createFlacStemResolver API and its exact range behavior. Do not copy the controller or expose source internals at package entrypoints.

The existing public ReadableStream path currently sends output-credit on enqueue. B needs a PRIVATE borrowed-output path through that SAME queue: `{bytes, release}` where release sends credit exactly once after all mapped slices are consumed; cancellation releases/discards ownership without a late worker message. Legacy ReadableStream adapter can preserve its existing enqueue semantics. Do not obtain B output by eagerly draining/copying that public stream. Keep two <=384KiB worker output credits, one256KiB input slot and existing2MiB decoder memory. Account for the original retained output buffer even when its views are <=128KiB. This is a real bounded controller change: accepted66's PCM admission and watchdog currently inspect only `blocks.length`, and its stream shifts a buffer then immediately credits it. In the private path the maximum-two count must include queued buffers PLUS the one buffer checked out to the span mapper; shifting cannot free a credit or resume the stall timer. Resume only when release actually returns credit. Cancellation/error discards queued and checked-out ownership exactly once, and late release after terminal worker settlement must not post a credit. Preserve the same queue, single input command lane and physical worker lifecycle; no parallel output controller or public stream drain. A small shared take/release primitive with a legacy stream wrapper and a private consumer is sufficient; if implementing it requires a wholesale controller rewrite, stop and rescope before layering acquisition on top.

Pass whole-source identity as diagnostics/context and chunk shape plus expected chunk PCM digest as distinct private decode context. Do not supply a chunk digest as a fake whole-source identity, compare chunk output to the whole source digest, or register a chunk as a verified canonical source. Always hash chunk packed PCM in the host with IncrementalSha256 for this slice, including with injected workers/assets. Worker digest is not trust authority. Enforce exact PCM bytes/frames and frame alignment regardless of optional legacy processing behavior. In particular, accepted66 currently enforces prepared totals only when options.processing exists; B must have an explicit private strict decode policy, independent of processing, and validate each PCM block frame count against its byte length as well as final chunk totals. Worker start keeps the parent identity, uses chunk shape, and disables whole-source worker-digest authority; host chunk digest verification remains mandatory.

Map packed frame offsets monotonically through admitted intervals. Split each borrowed block at interval boundaries AND largest frame-aligned size <=128KiB (stereo24 requires rounding). Each emitted `{startFrame,bytes}` is a view into the bounded original block; never materialize omitted gaps. One chunk can span several intervals and several chunks can occupy one interval. Advance exactly once and release the original output only after its final slice. Full packed endpoint must match interval/chunk totals.

## Completion, cancellation and Effect scope

Span done requires every chunk decoded with exact shape/count/host packed-PCM hash, each finite encoded extent/hash finished, mapped packed totals exact, and actual object EOF after the declared endpoint. A correct Content-Length never replaces EOF. All-silent manifests use zero workers but still read/admit the entire manifest and require object EOF. Store then hashes implicit gaps/final gap and active bytes against authoritative whole-source identity, closes data and publishes marker last. No sourceComplete/progress success or returned verified descriptor precedes the store's complete canonical verification.

Decoder frame completion does not report exact compressed parser-consumed position. Draining validates finite bytes/hash; it cannot prove semantic consumption of an intentionally declared, rehashed suffix. State this limitation plainly; no codec ABI expansion. Undeclared trailing bytes, truncation, or changed declared suffix without matching manifest hash must fail before span EOF.

Abort/return/error stops new input, interrupts actual HTTP, terminates active worker through existing pool ownership, settles source/iterator finalizers and releases admission. Store cleanup runs only after physical resource settlement. Terminal completion cannot enqueue late input or mutate a released borrow. Failure leaves no newly accepted cache marker; previously committed sources survive.

## Focused gates and file budget

Use synthetic fixtures and the existing test/packed-browser/OPFS machinery. No timing work or private artist data.

- Integrated cold install with actual small FLAC chunks covers mono16/stereo24, gaps, one chunk across intervals and multiple chunks in one interval. Reconstruct bounded cache windows versus a dense oracle, require full canonical hash and physical payload bytes equal active PCM. Count one GET, no Range/HEAD, sequential worker leases and no whole-object/chunk buffers. Warm reopen/install must call locator/fetch/worker zero times.
- Segmentation table splits header, manifest and metadata; absent Content-Length succeeds. Wrong/malformed exposed length, unsupported visible encoding,206, each-section truncation, trailing object byte and the concrete body-view limits refuse. Reuse accepted parser malformed/canonical/count gates instead of duplicating their corpus.
- Delayed encoded finish/EOF blocks span done and commit; mutate final compressed bytes after PCM completion, reject chunk PCM hash/shape/count mismatch, and reject final full-source hash mismatch. Custom worker digest cannot bypass host checks. All-silent success and trailing-byte failure both instantiate zero workers.
- Hold a >128KiB borrowed stereo24 block across multiple slices/gaps and stall the store: output credit stays withheld until final slice consumption, bounds remain fixed and cancellation settles it once. Focused cancellation at HTTP wait, worker admission/read/finish and pending store consumption plus injected quota failure proves no committed marker and admission/resource settlement. Reuse66 stale-credit/no-progress tests with only integration-specific additions.
- Run focused new/changed tests, typecheck/format/source policy and one full package check. Extend the existing packed Chromium fixture for one REAL packaged decoder -> indexed GET -> real OPFS cold/warm install, retaining the real-worker request/count/hash evidence. Do not substitute an injected descriptor map for this acquisition proof or add another harness/browser matrix.

Expected source: new src/stems/sparse-resolver.ts and one private full-response cursor module; narrow flac-resolver.ts/decoder-byte-source.ts production borrow/context seam; src/stems/index.ts exports. Touch flac-delivery.ts only for a small shared request-policy helper if needed. Tests: one focused sparse acquisition file, existing resolver tests where seam changes, existing packed-browser fixture, sparse contract docs and issue evidence. No new session/store/pump orchestration, worker protocol or decoder-C changes.

Main risks are actual Effect response lifetime, delayed encoded drain versus worker completion, output-credit timing, and extra manifest/network metadata accounting outside historical worker reservation. Record bounded manifest byte/text/parsed-index overhead separately; do not claim the old8MiB worker reservation covers up to8MiB encoded JSON plus its decoded structures. Enforce the concrete per-operation caps and existing admitted concurrent-body width. If this needs a second controller or broader subsystem, stop/rescope before implementing it.
